chunks: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Farisi said: Abu Sa'id al-Rumayhi related to me that Abd al-Aziz ibn Ishaq reported to us that Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Harun al-Wasiti said: Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Makki reported to me that Munif, the freedman of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, said: My master Ja'far ibn Muhammad related to me, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them).

He said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was praying, when a man passed in front of him, and one of his companions stopped him. When he finished his prayer, he asked him: 'Why did you stop the man?' He answered: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! He passed between you and the prayer niche.' He replied: 'Woe unto you! Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, is closer to me than anyone passing between me and Him.'
Chapter: The Names of Allah (Exalted) and the Difference between their meanings and the meanings of the names of created beings.

key_terms.أَقْرَبُ إِلَيَّ: Closer to me; a key theological term indicating divine proximity.
key_terms.الْمِحْرَابُ: The prayer niche or direction of prayer, often used metonymically for the space in front of the pray-er.
key_terms.بَابُ أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ: Chapter of the Names of Allah; indicates the thematic context of divine attributes.
key_terms.حَظَرَ: To block, hinder, or interfere with.
key_terms.يَخْطُرَ: To pass quickly or run across; used here to describe the transient nature of the man's movement.

ai.seo_question: What is the theological significance of a man passing in front of a praying Imam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Hasan (AS) uses the physical act of passing in front of a worshipper to illustrate the theological principle of divine proximity (*qurb*), arguing that since God is nearer to the believer than their jugular vein, no created being can truly obstruct that spiritual connection. This incident serves as a practical demonstration of negating spatial limitations (*hajr*) for Allah, distinguishing His transcendent nearness from the physical blocking (*hijab*) experienced by humans. The hadith reinforces the Shia scholarly view that divine attributes are unique and not analogous to created qualities, emphasizing that God’s presence is not confined by physical space or motion.
